title: SDKS Forge Toolkit: curated polyglot examples (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI) with streaming + retry ergonomics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a small, opinionated "forge" toolkit of ready-to-run starter examples that demonstrate best-practice SDK usage patterns across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (HTTP server), and a multi-platform CLI. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics, unified retry/backoff patterns, graceful cancellation, token-cost-friendly batching examples, and test harness snippets. These templates should be copy-paste runnable, include CI snippets, and be kept intentionally minimal for adoption by engineering customers and internal examples site.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable example repos or folders delivered: nextjs-edge-app, fastapi-streaming, go-http-llm, cli-multi-platform
Streaming examples show SDK-specific ergonomic patterns: AbortController for TS, context manager for Python, context.Context cancellation for Go
Retry/backoff policy is documented and implemented consistently across examples (exponential + jitter, idempotency hints where appropriate)
Each example contains a README with setup, local dev, integration test, and short note on unit token costs/benchmarks
CI workflow in each example builds and runs smoke tests using the integration test harness (mocked responses for CI)
Design doc and API snippets linked in README and referenced in SDK docs
At least one cross-language cookbook snippet demonstrating the same end-to-end feature (e.g., streaming chat with function-calling)
tasks: Draft minimal design doc outlining ergonomic decisions and code motifs (TS/Python/Go)
Implement Next.js example using edge runtime streaming + AbortController pattern
Implement FastAPI example with async generator streaming and contextmanager-based cancellation
Implement Go HTTP server example showing context.Context cancel + KV cache warmup snippet
Build small CLI (Go or TS) showing batching + retry flags and local mode for dev
Write integration test harness and CI config that runs smoke tests against mocked Redwood responses
Author READMEs and short migration notes for existing sample consumers
Collect feedback from PM and DevEx; iterate on ergonomics and naming
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — initial design doc draft uploaded to Confluence. Goal is to keep examples <200 LOC each and prioritise clarity over completeness.

2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Implemented prototype for Next.js edge streaming. Uses AbortController + incremental JSON tokens. Opened PR #214. Noted that Edge runtime requires polyfill for fetch streams in local dev; documented in README.
2026-03-11 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed design notes. Requested explicit note about billing implications of long-lived streams and recommended adding a per-route soft timeout example.

2026-03-12 Daniel Soto (DevEx): Reviewed FastAPI streaming example. Suggested using 'asynccontextmanager' to standardize cancellation, and add an example showing how to reuse the same client across routes for connection pooling.

2026-03-12 Arjun Patel: Updated README with per-route timeout patterns and small benchmark numbers (median latency for streaming chat ~120ms first-chunk on local GPU emulation). Added integration test that asserts chunked streaming order.
2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Flagging for design pass on UX wording and function-calling examples. Will add the PM-approved wording before merge.
notes: Key ergonomic decisions: (1) Expose cancel primitives idiomatically per language (AbortController / async context manager / context.Context), (2) Centralize retry constants into the examples' shared utilities and show how to override for critical paths, (3) Prefer simple JSONL streaming for examples and include a short section on structured output and validation.
risks: Examples diverging from mainline SDK if not maintained; mitigated by small smoke CI and periodic example QA task. Potential breaking changes if SDK streaming API surface changes — will pin to SDK minor version in examples and add migration notes.
next_steps: Finish Go server example, finalize CLI flags for retry/backoff, run cross-language cookbook test, incorporate PM/Design wording, and merge PRs. Schedule post-merge demo in DevEx office hours.
